newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turks protest closing of Islamic schools.
newsitem.headline: Turks protest closing of Islamic schools.

text.p: Thousands of Islamist protesters gathered in Ankara's main square on Tuesday to demonstrate against proposed secularist education reforms, witnesses said.
"Break the hands of those who try to lay a finger on the Koran," chanted the crowd, estimated by a Reuters correspondent at up to 5,000. Many waved Turkish flags.
Hundreds of police in full riot gear eyed the crowd, prepared to step in if the protesters pushed on, as planned, toward the parliament building.
Earlier, police arrested 55 people as they tried to approach military headquarters, state-run Anatolia news agency said.
Turkish police banned traffic from the centre of the capital to prevent the demonstrators from marching towards parliament.
Anatolian said police acted after convoys of cars carrying Islamist protesters began gathering at two main mosques in Ankara in the early morning.
The Islamists have said they would march on parliament to protest at government attempts to extend secularist school education in a bill that would effectively close religious schools.
The bill has strong support from the powerful military, which has pressed the government to move against what it says is a growing threat of Islamic activism, fuelled by religious schooling.
Eleven people were arrested at a demonstration against the plans outside an Istanbul mosque at the weekend.
